newsitem.title: UK: DLJ announces London private banking move.
newsitem.headline: DLJ announces London private banking move.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc (DLJ) said on Monday it had started a private banking operation in London.
DLJ, which bought British corporate finance boutique Phoenix Group in January for around 50 million pounds ($81.9 million), said the new group was part of London-based DLJ International Ltd.
Tom Dicker, 43, has been hired from another U.S. firm Morgan Stanley to build up the operation. Dicker told Reuters he had started two-and-a-half months ago and the group now totalled eight people.
But while Dicker's group may employ a total of 70 people when fully staffed, this is likely to take around two years, he said.
"There will be space for 30 professionals and 30 or 40 support staff," Dicker said.
While the emphasis of the business will be on high net worth individuals -- people with assets of more than a million dollars, medium and small sized institutions will also be targeted.

Marketing to new clients has so far taken a back seat to setting up asset allocation models and strategy as well as hiring the right staff. DLJ International is also setting up a trust operation in the Channel Island of Guernsey.
"We have to expand before we can go around to clients. You can't walk before you can run," Dicker said.
The group -- DLJ's first investment services group outside the U.S. -- will offer multi-currency discretionary money management, brokerage, managed funds and private equity funds.

It will not only target the UK but also continental Europe, the Middle East, Africa and South East Asia. But while the first international office, said Dicker, it will not be the last. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
